The '''78th Golden Globe Awards''' honored the best in [[2020 in American television|American television of 2020]], as well as film in [[2020 in film|2020]] and early [[2021 in film|2021]],<ref name="Timetable">{{cite web |url=https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/hfpa-announces-timetable-78th-golden-globe-awards |title=HFPA Announces the Timetable for the 78th Golden Globe Awards |publisher=[[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] |date=July 27, 2020 |access-date=November 10, 2020 |language=en |archive-date=August 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804162931/https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/hfpa-announces-timetable-78th-golden-globe-awards |url-status=live }}</ref> as chosen by the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] (HFPA). The ceremony took place on February 28, 2021, nearly two months later than normal, due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]] and [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on television|on television]].<ref name="Postponement">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/golden-globes-postponed-date-nbc-1234637007/ |title=Golden Globes 2021 Postponed Nearly Two Months |last=McNary |first=Dave |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 22, 2020 |access-date=February 2, 2021 |language=en |archive-date=June 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622192814/https://variety.com/2020/film/news/golden-globes-postponed-date-nbc-1234637007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Produced by [[Dick Clark Productions]] and the HFPA, and aired live on [[NBC]] in the United States, this was the first bi-coastal Golden Globes ceremony, with [[Tina Fey]] co-hosting from [[Rainbow Room|the Rainbow Room]] in [[New York City]], and [[Amy Poehler]] co-hosting from [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]].<ref name="Deadline">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2021/02/golden-globes-ceremony-bi-coastal-tina-fey-amy-poehler-new-york-los-angeles-1234685990/ |title=Golden Globes To Go Bicoastal For First Time; Live Show To Feature Tina Fey From New York, Amy Poehler From L.A. |last=Hipes |first=Patrick |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=February 2, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2021 |language=en |archive-date=February 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203000917/https://deadline.com/2021/02/golden-globes-ceremony-bi-coastal-tina-fey-amy-poehler-new-york-los-angeles-1234685990/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The nominees were announced on February 3, 2021. [[Jane Fonda]] and [[Norman Lear]] were announced as the recipients of the [[Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award|Cecil B. DeMille Award]] and the [[Carol Burnett Award]], respectively.<ref name="Fonda">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/awards/jane-fonda-golden-globes-cecil-b-demille-award-grace-and-frankie-1234891745/ |title=Jane Fonda to Receive Golden Globes' Cecil B. DeMille Award |last=Lang |first=Brent |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=January 26, 2021 |access-date=January 31, 2021 |archive-date=January 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128195540/https://variety.com/2021/film/awards/jane-fonda-golden-globes-cecil-b-demille-award-grace-and-frankie-1234891745/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Lear">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/golden-globes-norman-lear-to-receive-carol-burnett-award |title=Golden Globes: Norman Lear to Receive Carol Burnett Award |last=Feinberg |first=Scott |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=January 28, 2021 |access-date=January 31, 2021 |archive-date=January 30, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130060648/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/golden-globes-norman-lear-to-receive-carol-burnett-award |url-status=live }}</ref>

With 4 wins, ''[[The Crown (TV series)|The Crown]]'' won the most at the ceremony, including [[Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama|Best TV Series – Drama]]. ''[[Schitt's Creek]]'' and ''[[The Queen's Gambit (miniseries)|The Queen's Gambit]]'' won 2 each, with the former winning [[Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy|Best TV Series – Musical or Comedy]] and the latter winning [[Golden Globe Award for Best Limited or Anthology Series or Television Film|Best Miniseries or TV Film]]. In film, ''[[Borat Subsequent Moviefilm]]'', ''[[Nomadland (film)|Nomadland]]'', and ''[[Soul (2020 film)|Soul]]'' won 2 each, with ''Nomadland'' winning [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama|Best Motion Picture – Drama]] and ''Borat'' winning [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy|Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy]].

==Production==
[[Tina Fey]] and [[Amy Poehler]] were announced as the hosts of the ceremony, for the fourth time, in January 2020,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/tina-fey-and-amy-poehler-hosts-78th-golden-globes |title=Tina Fey and Amy Poehler: Hosts of the 78th Golden Globes |publisher=[[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] |date=January 12, 2020 |access-date=November 10, 2020 |language=en |archive-date=April 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401231004/https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/tina-fey-and-amy-poehler-hosts-78th-golden-globes |url-status=live }}</ref> but for the very first time to co-host the Golden Globes bicoastally, both from [[Manhattan]] and from [[Beverly Hills, California]]. By June 2020, the HFPA decided to postpone the ceremony from its normal date in early January to February 28 due to both the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]] and [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on television|on television production]].<ref name="Timetable"/><ref name="Postponement"/> On February 2, 2021, it was reported that the ceremony would be held from both the [[Rainbow Room]] in [[New York City]] and the Golden Globes' usual home at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in Beverly Hills, California, allowing those on the [[East Coast of the United States|East Coast]] to participate without having to make the cross-country trip.<ref name="Deadline"/> The nominees were announced on February 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/03/entertainment/golden-globe-nominations/index.html |title=Golden Globes 2021: See the full list of nominees |last=France |first=Lisa Respers |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=February 3, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2021 |language=en |archive-date=February 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204213129/https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/03/entertainment/golden-globe-nominations/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/feb/03/golden-globes-2021-nominations-a-new-thoughtfulness-in-the-air |title=Golden Globes 2021 nominations: 'A new thoughtfulness in the air' |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=February 3, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2021 |language=en |archive-date=November 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120171132/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/feb/03/golden-globes-2021-nominations-a-new-thoughtfulness-in-the-air |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Timetable==
* The eligibility period for motion pictures was extended to February 28, 2021.<ref name="Timetable"/>

===Cecil B. DeMille Award===
The [[Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award|Cecil B. DeMille Award]] is an honorary award bestowed to honorees who have made a significant mark in the film industry. It is named after its first recipient, director [[Cecil B. DeMille]].

* [[Jane Fonda]]<ref name="Fonda"/>

===Carol Burnett Award===
The [[Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award|Carol Burnett Award]] is an honorary award given for outstanding and lasting contributions to television on or off the screen. It is named in honor of its first recipient, actress [[Carol Burnett]].

* [[Norman Lear]]<ref name="Lear"/>

==Ceremony==

===Golden Globe Ambassadors===
The [[Golden Globe Ambassador]]s are Jackson Lee and Satchel Lee, the son and daughter of [[Spike Lee]] and [[Tonya Lewis Lee]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/awards/golden-globes/golden-globes-ambassador-2021-spike-lee-kids/ |title=Spike Lee's kids named 2021 Golden Globe Ambassadors |last=Nolfi |first=Joey |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=January 12, 2021 |access-date=January 31, 2021 |archive-date=January 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113070646/https://ew.com/awards/golden-globes/golden-globes-ambassador-2021-spike-lee-kids/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Reception==

===Critical response===
According to the [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]], which sampled 15 critic reviews and calculated a [[weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average score]] of 35 out of 100, the ceremony received "generally unfavorable reviews".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-golden-globe-awards/season-78 |title=The Golden Globe Awards: Season 78 |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-date=March 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302003842/https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-golden-globe-awards/season-78 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], 10% of 21 critics have given the ceremony a positive review, with an average rating of 3.52/10. The critics consensus on the website reads: "Disappointingly dull and disturbingly lacking in self-awareness, The 78th Golden Globes ceremony wastes its menagerie of celebrities—and some well-deserved wins—on a stilted ceremony overshadowed by HFPA's questionable behind-the-scenes behavior."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/golden_globes/s78 |title=Golden Globes: 78th Golden Globe Awards (2021) |publisher=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-date=March 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301042025/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/golden_globes/s78 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Controversies===
The ceremony received criticism regarding certain nominations. [[James Corden]]'s nomination for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy|Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy]] (for his performance in ''[[The Prom (film)|The Prom]]'') and the two nominations for ''[[Emily in Paris]]'' have faced controversy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/golden-globes-james-corden-nominated-reactions-b1797475.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204095401/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/golden-globes-james-corden-nominated-reactions-b1797475.html |archive-date=2021-02-04 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |title='A joke': Critics furious over controversial Golden Globe nominations |last=O'Connor |first=Roisin |work=[[The Independent]] |date=February 4, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/tv/a35633677/emily-in-paris-golden-globes-controversy/ |title=Why Netflix's 'Emily in Paris' Is Creating So Much Controversy at the Golden Globes |last=Bonner |first=Mehera |work=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]] |date=February 26, 2021 |access-date=February 26, 2021 |archive-date=February 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226233905/https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/tv/a35633677/emily-in-paris-golden-globes-controversy/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association|HFPA]] also drew criticism for the placement of ''[[Minari (film)|Minari]]'' in the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] category, despite being an American film about a [[Korean Americans|Korean-American]] family; it ultimately won.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/golden-globes-minari-wins-foreign-language-award-after-being-barred-from-best-picture-category |title=Golden Globes: 'Minari' Wins Foreign Language Award After Being Barred From Best Picture Category |last=Galuppo |first=Mia |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=February 28, 2021 |access-date=March 4, 2021 |archive-date=March 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301030531/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/golden-globes-minari-wins-foreign-language-award-after-being-barred-from-best-picture-category |url-status=live }}</ref> The determination that the film would be eligible for this category rather than [[Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama|Best Motion Picture – Drama]], based on the Globes' rule that any film with over 50% of its dialogue not in English would be considered a Foreign Language Film, invited controversy.<ref name="Vulture">{{cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2020/12/minari-golden-globes-2021-controversy-explained.html |title=The Golden Globes' ''Minari'' Controversy, Explained |last=Jones |first=Nate |work=Vulture |date=December 23, 2020 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-us |archive-date=December 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201223212513/https://www.vulture.com/2020/12/minari-golden-globes-2021-controversy-explained.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2021/02/11/minari-american-film-even-if-golden-globes-disagree/4340916001/ |title=Here's why 'Minari' is truly an American story, even if the Golden Globes disagree |last=Ryu |first=Jenna |work=[[USA Today]] |date=February 11, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-US |archive-date=February 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211161037/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/movies/2021/02/11/minari-american-film-even-if-golden-globes-disagree/4340916001/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/dec/26/hollywood-minari-american-film-golden-globes |title=Outcry in Hollywood over Minari's placement in foreign-language category |last=Helmore |first=Edward |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=December 26, 2020 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=December 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201226143318/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/dec/26/hollywood-minari-american-film-golden-globes |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.com/golden-globes-snubs-minari-over-183529067.html |title=Golden Globes Snubs 'Minari' Over Controversial Foreign Language Rule |last=Ke |first=Bryan |publisher=[[Yahoo! News]] |date=February 4, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-US |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210208233122/https://news.yahoo.com/golden-globes-snubs-minari-over-183529067.html |archive-date=February 8, 2021 }}</ref> [[Lulu Wang (filmmaker)|Lulu Wang]], whose film ''[[The Farewell (2019 film)|The Farewell]]'' was subject to the same rule the [[77th Golden Globe Awards|previous year]], wrote that "I have not seen a more American film than #Minari this year. It's a story about an immigrant family, IN America, pursuing the American dream. We really need to change these antiquated rules that characterize American as only English-speaking".<ref name="Vulture" /> Author [[Viet Thanh Nguyen]] wrote that the "decision speaks powerfully to the issue of what makes something — a language or a person or a culture — foreign".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/outlook/2020/12/24/minari-foreign-american-language/ |title='Minari' is about immigrants who speak Korean. That doesn't make it 'foreign.' |last=Nguyen |first=Viet Thanh |author-link=Viet Thanh Nguyen |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=December 24, 2020 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286 |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201224113635/https://www.washingtonpost.com/outlook/2020/12/24/minari-foreign-american-language/ |archive-date=December 24, 2020 }}</ref> Many other filmmakers, actors, and authors, including [[Nia DaCosta]], [[Daniel Dae Kim]], [[Min Jin Lee]], [[Franklin Leonard]], [[Simu Liu]], [[Phil Lord and Christopher Miller|Phil Lord]], [[Celeste Ng]], [[Harry Shum Jr.]], and [[Phillipa Soo]] criticized the decision on similar grounds.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/minari-foreign-language-film-golden-globes-1234874332/ |title=Hollywood Slams Golden Globes for Categorizing 'Minari' as Foreign Language Film: 'Enough of This Nonsense' |last=Lee |first=Janet W. |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=December 23, 2020 |access-date=February 22, 2021 |language=en-US |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201223191529/https://variety.com/2020/film/news/minari-foreign-language-film-golden-globes-1234874332/ |archive-date=December 23, 2020 }}</ref>

The nominations for the film ''[[Music (2021 film)|Music]]'' also faced criticism for the casting of [[Maddie Ziegler]] as an [[autism|autistic]] person, and concerns over what impact the film could have on the [[Global perceptions of autism|perception]] and [[Autism rights movement|handling]] of autistic people,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/news/sia-music-autism-golden-globes-twitter-b1797493.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204103337/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/news/sia-music-autism-golden-globes-twitter-b1797493.html |archive-date=2021-02-04 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |title=Sia apologises over controversial Music scenes and deactivates Twitter account: 'I listened to the wrong people' |last=O'Connor |first=Roisin |work=[[The Independent]] |date=February 4, 2021 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> with co-host [[Tina Fey]] joking that "[[Twitter]] is saying it's the most offensive casting since [[Kate Hudson]] was the [[WW International|Weightwatchers]] spokesperson".<ref name="Monologue">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/golden-globes-2021-best-jokes-b1808955.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301011708/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/golden-globes-2021-best-jokes-b1808955.html |archive-date=2021-03-01 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |title=Golden Globes 2021: Amy Poehler and Tina Fey take aim at James Corden and Sia in fiery monologue |last=White |first=Adam |work=[[The Independent]] |date=March 1, 2021 |access-date=March 3, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Hosts Fey and [[Amy Poehler]] also acknowledged the recent revelation that the HFPA has not had a single Black member for over twenty years.<ref name="Monologue" />

===Viewership===
The ceremony received 6.9 million viewers in the United States, with a 1.5 [[Nielsen ratings|Nielsen rating]] among adults 18 to 49, representing a 68% drop in viewership from the [[77th Golden Globe Awards|previous year's ceremony]]. It is the least viewed Golden Globe Awards telecast since the [[65th Golden Globe Awards]] in 2008, which was solely a press conference due to the [[2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike]].<ref name="Ratings"/>
